summary: Iteration 5 confirmed that including block_size_in_tokens as a searchable parameter (correcting iter-4's omission) dramatically amplifies NSGA-II's advantage over random search: NSGA-II crossed 95% of exhaustive hypervolume at eval ~109 while random never reached 95% within 200 evals — a gap of >91 evals versus the predicted >60 and iter-4's 47. The main surprise was how sparse the Pareto front turned out to be (4.5% of 1800 configs, vs predicted 15–22%), caused by block_size=32 and higher-TP configs cascading to dominate a much larger fraction of the space than modeled.
key_points: NSGA-II advantage confirmed and amplified: NSGA-II reached 99.2% of exhaustive HV at eval 200 vs random's 94.3%; the convergence gap (~91 evals) substantially exceeded both the predicted >60-eval threshold and iter-4's 47-eval gap, validating that the block_size × kv_blocks × TP interaction gives the evolutionary crossover operator exploitable structure.

Pareto front far sparser than expected: Only 4.5% of 1800 configs (81 configs) are Pareto-optimal, vs the predicted 15–22%. The 81 optimal configs cluster tightly in a narrow band — high TP (tp=4 or tp=8), block_size=32, low kv_blocks, batch≥256 — because block_size=32 dominance cascades were much stronger than modeled (bs=32 at lower kv_blocks beats bs=16 at higher kv_blocks when throughput is similar).

Key mechanism validated: block_size=32 at tp=8/kv=3000 delivers a 92× TTFT improvement (25ms vs 2323ms) because effective KV capacity (3000×32=96k tokens) clears the saturation threshold that block_size=16 (48k tokens) cannot. This single interaction was the root cause of iter-4's flawed reduced-space assumption.

Still unknown — rate portability: All iter-5 experiments used rate=50 req/s. Validation runs at rate=100 showed even stronger saturation differentiation (rps drops from 26.78 to 8.54 for under-resourced configs), but no algorithm comparison has been run at this rate. It is unknown whether NSGA-II's advantage persists, grows, or shrinks when the stress level changes.

Recommended next iteration (iter-6): Run algorithm comparison at rate=100 to test portability of the findings. Optionally replace raw total_kv_blocks with effective KV memory (blocks × block_size) as the cost objective, which would better reflect real resource consumption and may expose new Pareto structure.
